_readme: Models are Wavefront OBJ files (metres, Y up, -Z is the front of cars and the tram). Each .obj has a .mtl next to it. Every file here is listed below with a note.

Edit them in Blender: File > Import > Wavefront (.obj), change the model, then File > Export > Wavefront (.obj) over the same file. Keep 'Write Materials' on, Forward axis -Z, Up axis Y, and keep the file name.

Materials: Kd is the colour, Ke the glow, d the opacity, map_Kd a PNG from assets/textures. Leading words of a material name switch behaviour: unlit_ (no shading), glass_ (see-through), phong_ (shiny), dbl_ (two-sided), vcol_ (vertex colours), alpha40_ (cut-out). Full list at the top of js/render/obj.js.
Some material names are filled in by the game per copy (car paint, the picture on a sign, the facade of a house...). Their colour or texture in the file is only a stand-in; the notes below say which.
An object whose name ends in .nocast does not cast a shadow. In cars, objects named opt.* are optional extras the game adds at random; 'shadowpad' is the soft shadow under a car or tram.
Houses are assembled from the buildings/ kit: wall bays (3.0 x 3.2 m slabs), roofs for 6 and 9 m wide houses (9 m deep), shopfront, door, awning and so on. See js/models/buildings.js.

Add a new model: put the .obj and .mtl in a folder here, list it in this file, and load it with __tram.model('folder/name'). New landmarks are picked up automatically (landmarks/<name>.obj, then use <name> in js/world/zones.js).
vehicles/tram: The De Lijn HermeLijn tram of Ghent: five sections with bellows, 29.6 m long, both ends identical. 'dest' is the destination display (the game picks a tram-dest-N texture per tram); tram-side and tram-front carry the livery; the pantograph reaches the wire at 5.9 m. 'shadowpad' is the soft shadow.

vehicles/car-door-hatch: Front door of the 'hatch' (the one that swings open on parked cars). The origin is the hinge.

props/trash-paper: Flyer on the ground (slot 'paper' = paper colour).

props/parked-bike: Parked bike facing -Z. 'frame' = frame colour (the game picks one per bike).
props/road-sign: Square Belgian road sign on a pole; 'sign_face' is replaced by the picture of each sign (textures/signs/road-*.png).
props/road-sign-tall: Tall road sign (zone 30 / LEZ) on a pole; 'sign_face' is replaced per sign.
props/type-sign: Street-type sign on a pole; 'sign_face' is replaced per street type (textures/signs/type-*.png).
props/tram-stop: Tram/bus shelter with the stop flag. 'stop_sign' is the flag face (tram or bus).
props/stop-kerb: Raised tram stop platform edge, 6 m long, along Z.
props/blade-sign: Hanging shop blade sign on its bracket; 'blade_face' is replaced per shop (textures/shops/blade-*.png).
props/traffic-cone: Traffic cone with reflective band and base.
props/pothole: Pothole with a rim of rubble.
props/roadworks-sign: Roadworks warning sign on a tripod.
props/roadworks: Roadworks pit with barrier and four cones (the worker is added by the game). 'lamp' is the flashing lamp the game animates.
props/coin: Euro coin pickup, standing upright (the game spins it).

props/hedge-18: Villa garden hedge with gate pillars and fence, 18 m wide along Z.
props/hedge-21: Villa garden hedge with gate pillars and fence, 21 m wide along Z.

landmarks/msk: Museum voor Schone Kunsten: long pale neoclassical front, a deep colonnade at the entrance, statues on the attic. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'msk'.
landmarks/oudepost: Oude Postgebouw on the Korenmarkt: pale neo-gothic block with a slender corner tower and a steep slate roof. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'oudepost'.
landmarks/graslei: Graslei guild houses: Spijker, Korenstapelhuis, Tolhuisje, Vrije Schippers, Korenmetershuis. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'graslei'.
landmarks/michiels: Sint-Michielskerk: gothic church whose tower was never finished, so it stops flat. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'michiels'.
landmarks/ntgent: NTGent: three raised central bays, a mosaic in the rounded tympanum, four statues, bronze figure on top. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'ntgent'.
landmarks/opera: Opera Gent: long classical front with arched ground floor, columns above and a balustrade. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'opera'.
landmarks/vooruit: Vooruit: eclectic brick-and-stone festival hall with a big arched window between two towers. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'vooruit'.
landmarks/vleeshuis: Groot Vleeshuis: long medieval hall, steep roof full of dormers, stepped gables at the ends. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'vleeshuis'.
landmarks/dokcrane: Dok Noord: blue harbour crane on a portal, the kind that still stands at the old docks. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'dokcrane'.
landmarks/fabriek: Dok Noord: old factory hall with a sawtooth roof and a brick chimney. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'fabriek'.
landmarks/belfort: Belfort (belfry) with the golden dragon and the four clock faces. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'belfort'.
landmarks/niklaas: Landmark 'niklaas'. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'niklaas'.
landmarks/baafs: Landmark 'baafs'. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'baafs'.
landmarks/stadshal: Stadshal: a 40 m open canopy, two parallel steep pitched roofs side by side, timber gable ends, a skin of glass shingles on four concrete corner piers. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'stadshal'.
landmarks/boekentoren: Boekentoren: the tall concrete library tower. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'boekentoren'.
landmarks/station: Landmark 'station'. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'station'.
landmarks/gravensteen: Gravensteen: castle with corner towers. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'gravensteen'.
landmarks/kiosk: Landmark 'kiosk'. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'kiosk'.
landmarks/crane: Landmark 'crane'. Placed by js/world/zones.js under the name 'crane'.
props/bike-basket: Wooden carrier box the game adds to some parked bikes (same coordinates as props/parked-bike).
buildings/bay-window: One facade bay with a window: a 3.0 m wide x 3.2 m tall wall slab, 0.25 m thick, facing +X (the front face is at x = 0, the slab goes back to x = -0.25). 'facade_win' on the front face is replaced by the facade texture (the layered wall + window PNGs in textures/facades); the grey material is the hidden back, top and bottom. The two short ends are open on purpose: neighbouring bays close them. Walls are stacked from these.
buildings/bay-blank: One blank facade bay (no window), a 3.0 x 3.2 m wall slab, 0.25 m thick, facing +X, built like bay-window. 'facade_blank' is replaced by the matching wall texture. Used for side walls and shop ground floors.
buildings/plinth-bay: Hardstone plinth for one bay (3 m along Z), on the front wall plane.
buildings/shopfront: Shopfront box, 5.5 m wide (two bays minus a pilaster each side). 'shop_face' is replaced by the shop picture (textures/shops/shopfront-*.png).
buildings/door: Front door with frame, fanlight, knob and step, centred in a bay. 'door_leaf' = door colour (green or brown, picked per house).
buildings/awning: Shop awning over a 2-bay shopfront, tilted. 'awning' is replaced by one of textures/shops/awning-*.png.
buildings/poster: Party poster on a student house; 'poster_face' is replaced by textures/student/poster-*.png.
buildings/chimney: Brick chimney, origin at its middle.
buildings/hoist: Warehouse hoist beam and loading door for a stepped-gable house (house coordinates, wall top at y = 0).
buildings/roof-flat-6: Flat roof with coping for a 6 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-step-6: Stepped gable roof for a 6 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-bell-6: Bell gable roof with round window for a 6 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-cornice-6: Cornice with a mansard roof and two dormers for a 6 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-pitch-6: Pitched roof, gable towards the street for a 6 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture. 'roof_main' = slate or tile (picked per house).
buildings/roof-flat-9: Flat roof with coping for a 9 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-step-9: Stepped gable roof for a 9 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-bell-9: Bell gable roof with round window for a 9 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-cornice-9: Cornice with a mansard roof and two dormers for a 9 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-pitch-9: Pitched roof, gable towards the street for a 9 m wide house, 9 m deep. y = 0 is the top of the wall. 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture. 'roof_main' = slate or tile (picked per house).
buildings/roof-pitch-dormer: Dormer window on a pitched roof (house coordinates, wall top at y = 0). 'facade_blank' = the house's wall texture.
buildings/roof-saw-bay: One sawtooth roof tooth with its skylight, 3 m x 3 m (industrial halls are tiled from these). y = 0 is the top of the wall.
buildings/villa-roof: Unit hip roof (a four-sided pyramid, radius 1, height 1, corners on the X and Z axes); the game scales it to each villa and turns it 45 degrees.
buildings/villa-dormer: Dormer on a villa roof (house coordinates relative to the front wall plane, roof base at y = 0). 'facade_blank' = wall texture.
buildings/villa-porch: Villa porch: white columns, roof, three steps and the front door, on the front wall plane (x = 0).
